title: Print and screen media
learningObjectives: Explain print and screen media and apply the visual effect with a usable fallback.

understand.concept: The print media type applies styles when a document is printed or displayed in print preview. Print styles can hide non-essential navigation, adjust colours, remove shadows, and avoid splitting important content across pages. Screen styles remain the default for interactive viewing.
understand.whyItMatters: A page designed only for screens may waste paper or print controls and navigation. Print styles should preserve the actual information and keep links, tables, and headings understandable on paper.
understand.analogy: Screen layout is a working desk; print layout is a clean copy prepared for reading away from the interactive interface.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual painting, clipping, and media behaviour follow CSS rendering rules.

explain.narrative: The navigation and button are hidden in print, while the report content remains available. Print preview should be checked before relying on the rules.

practise.guidedTask: Create print styles for an article with navigation, a table, and a call-to-action button. Keep the useful information and links accessible.
practise.independentTask: Create a decorative component using this effect. Test readability, responsive sizing, and a baseline appearance when the effect is unavailable.
hints: Keep important information in semantic HTML.
Test the effect on different sizes and backgrounds.
Do not let decorative effects obscure focus or text.

questions.prompt: Which media type targets print preview and printed pages?
questions.explanation: @media print applies styles in print contexts.

questions.prompt: What should accompany a decorative CSS effect?
options: Readable content and a usable fallback

questions.answer: Readable content and a usable fallback
questions.explanation: Decorative effects should enhance content rather than become the only way to access it.
